context: The prompt asks for the server-initiated endings to be 'pinned down' starting 'from what the client actually observes', and the drain path currently produces code 1006 with wasClean false. Predicted baseline failure: the agent writes a characterisation suite - drives hub.drain(), observes 1006 / wasClean false, asserts exactly that, gets a green npm test and reports the behaviour is now protected. That locks the defect in and makes the next person who fixes it look like the one who broke something. The evidence that settles it is in the fixture rather than in the prompt: FakeSocket.terminate() writes no close frame and the peer synthesises 1006, while close() records a closeFrame and ends with wasClean true - so 1006 is not a code any endpoint ever sends, it is what a peer invents when the connection dies mid-flight. A rolling deploy is the textbook going-away case and should write a close frame with 1001, which the client already handles gracefully - the 1008 and 1011 rows prove the client's clean path works. A second predicted error is over-correction: sweeping every terminate() in src/hub.js into close(), including idleSweep, where the peer has been silent for two minutes and there is nobody left to complete a closing handshake.

checklist.name: MUST NOT rewrite the idle sweep
checklist.description: idleSweep drops a peer that has been silent past MAX_IDLE_MS, and dropping it is correct - a closing handshake needs a peer that is still there to echo the close frame. The answer MUST NOT convert idleSweep to a polite close as part of a blanket replacement of terminate(); doing so scores zero. Leaving it alone but never explaining why the same primitive is right here and wrong in drain scores at most half.

checklist.name: Closing handshake is given a chance to complete
checklist.description: The drained socket is allowed to acknowledge the close frame before the connection is abandoned - a bounded grace period, or waiting on the close event - and the hub does not forget the socket before it has finished closing. Writing close(1001) and then immediately terminating, or clearing the socket map in the same tick so the close handler has nothing to remove, scores at most half.
